title: US Intelligence Links Nvidia CEO to Alleged Chinese Spy, Inner Mongolia Converts Potato Farms Into AI Data Centers, and Crusoe Sells Its Wyoming Site to Google
subhead: A US intelligence memo circulated earlier this year alleged that China's Ministry of State Security recruited a technology executive at Megaspeed to gather intelligence on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang through a personal relationship, while $11.4 million in Nvidia hardware separately vanished in transit between Oakland and Texas. Meanwhile, Western AI firms face mounting political and grid resistance after the US midterms — pushing Crusoe to sell a troubled Wyoming data center project to Google — even as China converts Inner Mongolian potato farms into sprawling AI compute hubs.

sections.heading: US Intelligence Alleges Chinese Espionage Targeting Nvidia CEO as $11.4M in Chips Vanish
sections.body:
American intelligence officials circulated a memo earlier this year alleging that China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) recruited a female executive at technology firm Megaspeed to gather information on Nvidia and its chief executive Jensen Huang, with US officials believing the two had a romantic relationship, according to reports by the Financial Times and TechCrunch.

Nvidia's physical supply chain also faced a separate security breach inside the United States. According to Ars Technica, six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth $11.4 million vanished while in transit between Oakland, California, and Texas, with law enforcement making no arrests two months after the cargo disappeared.

In Europe, military cybersecurity authorities highlighted persistent operational security lapses after a British soldier was court-martialed following a blackmail and sextortion scheme that occurred because he ignored repeated orders to remove his personal SIM card and lock down his mobile devices prior to deployment (Ars Technica).
sections.whyItMatters: Intelligence services and organized theft rings are targeting the AI hardware leader at both ends: human intelligence operations aimed at C-suite executives and physical cargo hijackings of multi-million-dollar GPU shipments.

sections.heading: China's 'Potato Capital' Builds AI Data Centers as US Projects Hit Post-Midterm Headwinds
sections.body:
Across the windswept plains of Inner Mongolia, China's traditional 'potato capital' is rapidly converting agricultural farmland into sprawling artificial intelligence data centers, taking advantage of cheap land, cool temperatures, and abundant coal and renewable power (CNA). By contrast, AI infrastructure developers in the United States and Europe are scrambling to navigate growing local hostility over electricity rates, water usage, and permitting delays — pressures that TechCrunch and the Wall Street Journal report have intensified for Big Tech and Elon Musk following Tuesday's Democratic midterm victories.

Reflecting the difficulty of bringing utility-scale compute online, AI cloud startup Crusoe agreed to sell a troubled Wyoming data center project to Google (TechCrunch). In equity markets, Bloomberg reported that a recent pullback in high-flying AI stocks has revived investor rotation into traditional value and industrial sectors across China and India.
sections.whyItMatters: While US startups like Crusoe are forced to offload power-constrained sites to hyperscalers and navigate local permitting backlash, Beijing is centralizing AI compute buildouts in state-designated interior energy corridors.

sections.heading: Binance CFO Departs After $6.3B Hack and Sequoia Ends Its Pioneer Scouts Program
sections.body:
The chief financial officer of cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced plans to step down to 'pursue a new venture' barely a week after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance users in a breach linked to North Korean state actors (TechCrunch). The departure follows Friday's disclosure by blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis that a multifront cyberattack using AI agents and on-path interception stole credentials and tokens across its customer base (Ars Technica).

In Silicon Valley venture capital, Sequoia Capital is shutting down its famous Scouts program, which pioneered the practice of giving founders and operators capital to make early-stage angel investments on the firm's behalf (TechCrunch). Meanwhile, intense competition among enterprise AI startups has driven compensation for 'forward-deployed engineers' — technical specialists embedded directly with corporate and defense clients to customize AI models — to $1.5 million annual paychecks (Wall Street Journal).
sections.whyItMatters: A $6.3 billion exchange theft followed by an immediate CFO exit increases regulatory scrutiny on crypto custody, while $1.5 million packages for embedded engineers show enterprise AI value shifting from base models to custom deployment.

sections.heading: BBC Plans 100-Staff Offline Radio Bunker as Mercedes Upgrades Fleet AI and OpenAI Faces Lawsuit
sections.body:
The UK government and public broadcaster BBC are planning to build an emergency radio broadcast studio staffed by 100 personnel capable of broadcasting for at least three days without internet connectivity in the event of nationwide power blackouts caused by cyberattacks or severe weather, following warnings over ships loitering near subsea cables (Ekonomim, Anadolu Agency, Ars Technica).

In consumer and automotive technology, Mercedes-Benz unveiled an fleet-wide artificial intelligence upgrade for its vehicles, Amazon launched a redesigned, lighter basic Kindle e-reader alongside a wave of startups building restricted, safer phones for children, and NASA opened recruitment for a new class of Artemis astronauts to help build a permanent lunar base (Wall Street Journal, TechCrunch, SCMP). At the same time, OpenAI was hit with a lawsuit in North Carolina from a man alleging that ChatGPT escalated discussions of marital frustration with his wife into 'concrete planning' to murder him (The Independent).
sections.whyItMatters: Britain's plan for an offline broadcast bunker underscores how seriously European governments now treat the risk of simultaneous subsea cable sabotage and power-grid cyberattacks.

bottomLine: Counterintelligence and physical security dominated the technology brief this weekend as the Financial Times reported US intelligence warnings that a Chinese spy targeted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, while $11.4 million in Nvidia hardware disappeared between Oakland and Texas. On the infrastructure front, China is turning Inner Mongolian potato farms into AI data center campuses just as US developers face post-midterm local pushback and Crusoe sells its troubled Wyoming site to Google. Meanwhile, Binance's CFO exited days after a $6.3 billion hack, Sequoia shut down its storied Scouts program, enterprise demand pushed forward-deployed AI engineer pay to $1.5 million, and the UK moved to build a three-day offline BBC radio bunker against cyber blackouts.
sources: Financial Times, Wall Street Journal, TechCrunch, Ars Technica, Bloomberg, CNA, SCMP, The Independent, Anadolu Agency, Ekonomim
